# Designing for the bar

The screen is a 640 × 172 px strip, about 86 × 23 mm (7.5 px per mm), read at a glance and touched with a fingertip. It has two buttons and no keyboard. These patterns follow from that; the recipes in `recipes.md` implement them, and `ui_lint` checks the hard limits.

## Sizes in pixels and millimetres

| What | Pixels | Millimetres | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Whole screen | 640 × 172 | 86 × 23 | landscape only; the kit rotates for the panel |
| Smallest touch target | 56 × 56 | 7.5 | `LCD349_RULE_TOUCH_TARGET_PX`. Full-width list rows tagged `list-row` may be shorter |
| Smallest text | 12 tall | 1.6 | `LCD349_RULE_FONT_MIN_PX`. Body text is better at 14-20 px |
| Status bar band | 24 | 3.2 | title on the left; Wi-Fi, battery and time on the right |
| Body band | 148 | 19.7 | everything else; no third band |
| Side margin | 12 | 1.6 | keep text off the bezel |
| List row | 44-56 | 5.9-7.5 | about three rows show at once |
| Menu tile | 140 × 124 | 18.7 × 16.5 | four show across, the fifth peeks in to show there's more |

Convert with `LCD349_MM_TO_PX(mm)`. Lay out with LVGL alignment (`lv_obj_align`, flex rows) rather than absolute positions where you can: a design that survives a different font is a design that won't clip.

## Layout

- **Two bands.** A thin status band on top and one body below. A third band (a footer) leaves too little body on a 172 px screen: put hints in the body or rely on the buttons' fixed meanings.
- **Use the width.** The long axis is the one with room: rows of tiles, a list on the left with detail on the right, a title on the left with the action button on the right where a thumb reaches.
- **One task per screen.** A bar has room for one idea. Split a flow into screens rather than shrinking it.
- **Truncate on purpose.** Give labels a fixed width and `LV_LABEL_LONG_MODE_DOTS` (one line) or a fixed size with `LV_LABEL_LONG_MODE_DOTS` (several lines). Wrapped text isn't truncated: in a fixed height it runs off. Text that runs off is a lint error; text that ends in "..." isn't.
- **Show more with a peek.** Let the next row or tile show a few pixels at the edge so it's clear the content scrolls.

## Type

- LVGL's Montserrat at 14 px for body text and 20 px for titles and buttons covers almost everything; enable each size in `sdkconfig.defaults` (`CONFIG_LV_FONT_MONTSERRAT_14=y`). Add 28 px or larger only for one big number.
- The built-in fonts carry the `LV_SYMBOL_*` icons (Wi-Fi, battery, bell, settings...). A character the font lacks draws as nothing: `ui_lint` reports it (`missing-glyph`). Use plain ASCII or check accents.
- Don't go below the font rule even for hints: at 7.5 px per mm, 12 px is already only 1.6 mm tall.

## Colour and contrast

- The panel shows RGB565: 32 levels of red and blue, 64 of green. Gradients band visibly, so use flat colours (`ui_lint` warns on gradients whose ends differ).
- Text needs a 4.5:1 contrast with what's behind it, measured after the colours are reduced to RGB565. Light text on a dark background (`#0B1622` with white or `#B8C4D0`) passes easily and reads well outdoors.
- Use colour for state (accent for the selection, red for danger, green for done), never as the only signal: pair it with a word or an icon.

## Touch

- One finger, one point. No pinch, no multi-finger gestures, no long drags.
- Gestures go along the long axis: horizontal swipes move between tiles or pages. A vertical list works, but only about three rows fit.
- Turn kinetic scrolling off (`lv_obj_set_scroll_momentum(obj, false)`) and snap to items (`lv_obj_set_scroll_snap_x/y`). With full-frame flushes, momentum scrolling judders, and `ui_lint` reports it (`no-momentum`).
- LVGL gives every object "scroll on focus": a tap focuses the object and scrolls it into view. Turn it off on rows and tiles (`lv_obj_set_scroll_on_focus(obj, false)`) unless you want the list to move under the finger.
- Touch is sampled only while the display is on, and never wakes the board: a sleeping screen is woken with a button.

## The two buttons

- **Short press steps:** move the selection, next page, next item. A focus ring (an outline, or the accent fill on full-width rows) shows where you are.
- **Hold commits:** open, approve, confirm. Show the hold filling (the hold recipe), act when it completes, and let release cancel.
- **Chord** (both buttons) is for one rare, global action, such as back to home.
- **The visibility guard:** a hold commits only if the button went down at least 500 ms after the screen it confirms appeared, so a press meant for the previous screen can't approve this one.
- **Wake-only press:** when a button press wakes the board from sleep, that press only wakes it. Ignore gestures until both buttons are up again.
- **Never** design a boot-time combination with BOOT: held through a reset, it enters download mode instead of running the product.
- Button debouncing (10 ms) and hold timing are the kit's: use `lcd349_classifier_*`, not your own timers.

## Motion: step, don't animate

Every change costs a full-frame flush (about 13 ms). So:

- Change state at once. LVGL's default press transition alone costs about seven flushes per tap: give pressable objects a zero-length transition (`ui_no_press_animation` in the recipes; a NULL transition crashes LVGL 9.6).
- No fades, slides or spinners. A static "Working..." label is clearer and costs one frame.
- Redraw only what changed: set a label's text only when it differs, and move progress bars in steps (tenths), not every tick.

## Sleep and wake

- Dim, then sleep: lower the backlight after a short idle time, then `lcd349_display_sleep(true)` or `lcd349_sleep_until_button()` for light sleep. On the board, light sleep is still experimental (the kit's CHANGELOG lists its known problems): check it there.
- On wake, show the current state at once (no splash), and treat the waking press as wake-only.
- `lcd349_power_off()` powers the board off on battery; on USB it can't, and returns `LCD349_ERR_ON_USB`: tell the user.
- Storage (`lcd349_kv_*`) survives resets and power-off: save settings when they change, not at shutdown.
